title: Infra surge sprint notes - Rohan
content:
Context: quick personal runbook & sprint scratchpad for the surge window. Keep terse. Goal: stabilize tail latency <120ms 99th for hosted API during regional traffic spike, avoid large rebalances overnight.

Today (2026-03-13) plan:
- 06:30: quick health sweep (nodes, queues, kernel errors)
- 07:00: apply temporary scale policy on eu-west pool (scale +2 GPUs, pref Z2 racks)
- 07:15: enable conservative batching fallback on heavy routes (profiled routes: /chat-stream, /generate)
- 07:30: monitor KV hit-rate and eviction; enable prefix-cache warm for top-10 clients

Morning checklist (what I actually run) – tick when done:
- [ ] k8s pods: kubectl get pods -n infra --selector=pool=eu-west | grep CrashLoopBackOff (fix if present)
- [ ] check node disk pressure: kubectl describe node <node> | grep -i eviction
- [x] bump autoscaler min from 4->6 for eu-west-gpu-pool (temporary)
- [x] create short-lived alert: CPU percent > 75% for 2m -> slack @oncall
- [ ] open look for slow traces: trace-id filter: /api/v1/generate, 99p token-gen > 80ms

Helpful commands (copy/paste candidates):
- kubectl -n infra get pods -l pool=eu-west -o wide
- kubectl -n infra logs -f deployment/mini-infer --since=10m | grep -i error
- ssh ops@rack-node-23 "sudo journalctl -u nv-peer -n 200"
- curl -sS 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=token_latency&p90' | jq .

Quick triage notes (observations):
- noticed intermittent high KV miss rate on 07:05—likely cold starts after autoscale bump.
- two nodes reported nvlib warnings around 07:08; ticketed to INFRA-1289 for driver update regression.
- fallback batching reduced tail by ~15ms on snapshot tests; keep enabled for 30m and revisit.

Temporary mitigations tried and results:
- Enabled prefix-cache warm (seeded top 10 clients) -> KV hit-rate +12% in 10m, CPU steady.
- Forced placement away from Z1 racks for a noisy neighbor -> minor improvement, but reduced capacity for short window.

Action items (priority ordered):
1) Short: roll driver patch to suspect nodes (canary 2 nodes) -> if stable, roll next 6 in wave. Owner: Rohan. ETA: 3h.
2) Mid: add autoscaler policy threshold smoothing (increase scale-out threshold by +5s sustained request) and run smoke test. Owner: Platform-sre. ETA: EOD.
3) Long: evaluate KV eviction policy for prefix-cache (limit per-tenant) to avoid noisy tenant thrash. Owner: me + Leah. ETA: next sprint.

Notes to self / debugging hypotheses:
- hypothesis A: driver regression with newest cuda stack causes occasional slow memcpy on NVLink -> reproduce with synthetic load on canary node.
- hypothesis B: a specific large customer (acct: ACCT-493) is spiking with long sequences causing cache churn -> add per-tenant rate cap ramp to test.

Unresolved / questions to ask in standup:
- Do we want to prioritize driver rollback vs. kernel patch? (tradeoff: rollback faster but blocks queued PRs)
- Should we temporarily route ACCT-493 to dedicated pool to protect shared customers?

Hand-off notes for next shift:
- If driver canary fails (OOM or kernel warnings), immediate rollback plan: revert driver on canary nodes and scale down to min=4.
- If autoscaler thrashes, set cool-down to 180s and notify SRE channel.
- If KV miss rate > 35% for 10m, disable new prefix warm and re-evaluate seeding set.

Random reminders (personal):
- email Leah summary when baseline stable (~1hr window)
- capture a short recording of trace for INFRA-1289 before rolling drivers fleet-wide
- follow up with Omar on the PR gating logic for autoscaler change

End-of-day quick log (fill before closing):
- Stabilized? yes/no -> 
- Primary action taken -> 
- Anything carried to next day -> 

Scratchpad footer: this is a living capture — prune once notes turned into tickets/PRs.
